- Overestimate prices after recent spikes (especially if sentiment is positive or neutral) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative or shows recent downward momentum — model fails to capture downside risk.
- Lag in price correction: model often lags true price movements by 1–3 days, especially after sharp moves.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility and fails to smoothly revert to historical mean.
- Sentiment-driven bias: if sentiment is positive, model tends to over-forecast; if negative, under-forecast — adjust forecast by 5–10% downward if sentiment < 0.5, upward if sentiment > 1.0.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly sensitive to recent 7–14 day trends — reduce weight on recent spikes if sentiment is volatile.
